### ov.analysis.evidence.MODEL_CAPS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]* *= {'opus': (2576, 4784), 'standard': (1568, 1568)}*

(long-edge pixels, token cap). Opus 4.7/4.8 are larger.

* **Type:**
  Per-model image caps

### ov.analysis.evidence.build_evidence_bundle(run, store, , step_id=None, model='opus', task='Assess UX and architecture; cite marks/facts for every claim.', max_marks=20, overlay=True, out_dir=None)

Assemble a grounded [`EvidenceBundle`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.EvidenceBundle) for a step (model-free).

Marks are drawn from the step’s affordances (which carry bounding boxes);
facts include those marked regions plus the deterministic findings touching the
step. The token budget is computed against `model`’s cap. When Pillow is
available and `overlay` is set, a numbered overlay screenshot (and crops for
small regions) are rendered and stored; otherwise the original screenshot is
referenced and a note is recorded.

* **Return type:**
  [`EvidenceBundle`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.EvidenceBundle)

### ov.analysis.evidence.fit_to_cap(width, height, model='opus')

Project tokens and a downsample factor to fit a model’s image cap (pure).

Honors BOTH constraints – the long-edge pixel cap *and* the token (area) cap
– taking whichever is more restrictive, because a long-edge-only clamp can
still blow the token budget (a 2576x2576 image is ~8853 tokens).

```pycon
>>> r = fit_to_cap(5000, 4000, "opus")
>>> r["downsampled"] and r["fitted"]["tokens"] <= 4784
True
>>> fit_to_cap(800, 600, "opus")["downsampled"]
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ov.analysis.evidence.image_token_cost(width, height)

Anthropic image token estimate `ceil(w*h/750)`.

```pycon
>>> image_token_cost(1000, 1000)
1334
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### ov.analysis.evidence.png_dimensions(data)

Return `(width, height)` of a PNG from its IHDR header (stdlib only).

```pycon
>>> import base64
>>> px = base64.b64decode('iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAAC0lEQVR42mNk+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==')
>>> png_dimensions(px)
(1, 1)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.html.md

# ov.analysis

Analysis layer: deterministic analyzers over captured artifacts (Phases 2-3).

Analyzers are registered plugins (`ANALYZER_REGISTRY`) that read a
[`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun) plus its store and emit :class:

```
`
```

~ov.base.Finding\`s /
:class:

```
`
```

~ov.base.Endpoint\`s / facts – all model-free and fully testable on
synthetic artifacts. The host (or, later, an in-package agent) adds narrative
judgment *on top* of these via the evidence bundle.

Each analyzer is registered with a `lens` (`"ux"` or `"arch"`) so
`ov.analyze(run, lenses=...)` can select which to run; `requires`/`produces`
order them. The builtins are eagerly imported on first import of this package so
the registry is never half-populated (same robustness rule as the probes).

(The package is named `analysis` rather than `analyze` so it cannot shadow
the `ov.analyze` facade *function*; see `ov/__init__.py`.)

### Functions

| [`load_builtin_analyzers`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.html.md#ov.analysis.load_builtin_analyzers)()   | Import builtin analyzer modules so their `@register_analyzer` runs.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.analysis.load_builtin_analyzers()

Import builtin analyzer modules so their `@register_analyzer` runs.

Safe to call repeatedly. Invoked once at the bottom of this module so the
registry is fully populated on import (no order-dependent gaps).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### Modules

| [`arch`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.arch.html.md#module-ov.analysis.arch)               | Architecture-reconstruction analyzers (§6, D2).                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`context`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#module-ov.analysis.context)         | The analysis context + analyzer output -- the currency of the pure analyzers.   |
| [`diff`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.diff.html.md#module-ov.analysis.diff)               | Own-target diffing: a run vs a stored prior baseline run (review mode, §10).    |
| [`evidence`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.evidence.html.md#module-ov.analysis.evidence)       | The evidence-bundle assembler (§8.1, D4) -- deterministic, model-free.          |
| [`reliability`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#module-ov.analysis.reliability) | Reliability passes over findings (§5.2, D4) -- deterministic gates, model-free. |
| [`run`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.run.html.md#module-ov.analysis.run)                 | The analysis orchestrator -- resolve, order, run analyzers, merge into the run. |
| [`ux`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux)                   | UX + accessibility deterministic analyzers (§5.1, D3).                          |


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md

# ov.analysis.reliability

Reliability passes over findings (§5.2, D4) – deterministic gates, model-free.

These enforce the grounding discipline on findings (whether deterministic, or
authored by the host LLM over an evidence bundle):

* **cite-or-abstain** – every non-`undetermined` claim must cite at least one
  *resolvable* evidence ref; otherwise it is downgraded to `undetermined` (a
  first-class outcome, not an error).
* **set-of-mark membership** – any mark id a finding references must exist in the
  bundle.
* **just-in-time retrieval** – [`lookup_evidence()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.lookup_evidence) resolves an evidence id
  back to its artifact/finding/step so provenance is verifiable.
* **factored Chain-of-Verification scaffolding** – [`verification_questions()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.verification_questions)
  generates the questions the *host* answers (independently, via evidence lookup)
  for high-severity findings; [`apply_verification()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.apply_verification) downgrades a finding whose
  verification fails. The judgment is the host’s; the gating here is deterministic.

### Functions

| [`apply_verification`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.apply_verification)(finding, verdicts)        | Downgrade a finding to `undetermined` if a majority of verifications fail.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`lookup_evidence`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.lookup_evidence)(evidence_id, run, store)     | Resolve an evidence id back to its underlying data (just-in-time retrieval).           |
| [`resolvable`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.resolvable)(ref, run[, bundle])               | True if an evidence ref resolves to something concrete (artifact/finding/step/bundle). |
| [`verification_questions`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.verification_questions)(finding)              | Generate factored Chain-of-Verification questions for a high-severity finding.         |
| [`verify_findings`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.verify_findings)(findings, run, \*[, bundle]) | Apply cite-or-abstain + mark-membership; downgrade unsupported findings.               |

### Classes

| [`ReliabilityReport`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.ReliabilityReport)([kept, downgraded, notes])   | Outcome of [`verify_findings()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.verify_findings).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.analysis.reliability.ReliabilityReport(kept=list(), downgraded=list(), notes=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Outcome of [`verify_findings()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.verify_findings).

#### *property* all_findings *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[Finding](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding)]*

Kept + downgraded, in that order (nothing is silently dropped).

### ov.analysis.reliability.apply_verification(finding, verdicts)

Downgrade a finding to `undetermined` if a majority of verifications fail.

`verdicts` are the host’s independent answers (True = supported). This is the
deterministic application of the host’s factored CoVe / NLI judgments.

* **Return type:**
  [`Finding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding)

### ov.analysis.reliability.lookup_evidence(evidence_id, run, store)

Resolve an evidence id back to its underlying data (just-in-time retrieval).

Returns a dict describing what the id points at, so a verification pass (or a
downstream agent) can confirm a finding against the original artifact/record.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ov.analysis.reliability.resolvable(ref, run, bundle=None)

True if an evidence ref resolves to something concrete (artifact/finding/step/bundle).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ov.analysis.reliability.verification_questions(finding)

Generate factored Chain-of-Verification questions for a high-severity finding.

The host answers each *independently* (via [`lookup_evidence()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.lookup_evidence)), not
conditioned on the original claim – that’s what makes CoVe factored.

```pycon
>>> from ov.base import Finding
>>> qs = verification_questions(Finding(type="ux_issue", signal="contrast.text",
...     category="a11y", observed="contrast 2.1:1", evidence_refs=["art_1"]))
>>> len(qs) >= 2
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ov.analysis.reliability.verify_findings(findings, run, , bundle=None)

Apply cite-or-abstain + mark-membership; downgrade unsupported findings.

Deterministic findings (`source_layer == "deterministic"`) are facts and are
kept; LLM findings must cite resolvable evidence and reference only existing
marks. A finding that fails is downgraded to `undetermined` (kept, flagged),
never silently dropped.

#### NOTE
downgrading mutates the offending `Finding` in place (the caller
hands its findings in to be gated), so the objects in `report.downgraded` are
the same instances, now marked `undetermined` + `needs_human_review`.

* **Return type:**
  [`ReliabilityReport`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.reliability.html.md#ov.analysis.reliability.ReliabilityReport)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.run.html.md

# ov.analysis.run

The analysis orchestrator – resolve, order, run analyzers, merge into the run.

`run_analysis` is what [`ov.analyze()`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.analyze) calls. It selects analyzers by lens,
orders them by their `requires`/`produces` dependencies, runs each over an
[`AnalysisContext`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalysisContext), and merges every
[`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput) back into the `CaptureRun`
(findings, endpoints, tech, run fields). It is model-free and idempotent: it
clears prior analysis output before re-running so a run can be re-analyzed.

### Functions

| [`merge_output`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.run.html.md#ov.analysis.run.merge_output)(run, out)                         | Merge one analyzer's output into the run (findings, endpoints, tech, fields).           |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`run_analysis`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.run.html.md#ov.analysis.run.run_analysis)(run, \*[, lenses, store, config]) | Run the deterministic analyzers for `lenses` over a run; return per-analyzer summaries. |

### ov.analysis.run.merge_output(run, out)

Merge one analyzer’s output into the run (findings, endpoints, tech, fields).

Tech dedupes by name: confidence takes the max, provenance and categories
union (so a package seen both as a recovered dependency and by framework/bundler
signature keeps *both* category identities), and a missing version is filled
from any analyzer that supplies one (source-map versions are the top provenance
rank, so they must not be lost to an earlier versionless detection).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ov.analysis.run.run_analysis(run, , lenses=('ux', 'arch'), store=None, config=None)

Run the deterministic analyzers for `lenses` over a run; return per-analyzer summaries.

`run` may be a `CaptureRun` or a run id (loaded from `store`). The
run is mutated in place (findings/api_surface/fingerprint/rendering_model/…)
and persisted; an analysis blob is also stored.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.a11y.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.a11y

Accessibility analyzer: WebAIM perennials from the DOM + optional axe mapping.

The deterministic baseline parses each captured DOM state (`selectolax`) and
detects the WebAIM-Million perennials that are computable without a browser or a
GPL engine: missing image `alt`, empty links, empty buttons, unlabeled form
controls, and missing document language. These are ~96% of *detected* errors
(D3), so nailing them deterministically is high-value and fully testable.

If an `axe` artifact exists (an optional in-browser axe-core run at capture
time), its violations are additively mapped to Findings with `engine_rule_id`
`axe:<id>`. Contrast is handled by [`ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus) (it
needs computed colors, not static DOM).

**Honesty constraint (D3):** automated tooling catches only ~30-40% of WCAG
issues, so this analyzer always emits one `undetermined` finding routing the
non-automatable ~60-70% (meaningful alt text, reading/focus-order logicality,
in-context link text, screen-reader announcement quality, ARIA intent) to
`needs_human_review` – never asserting “no automated violations” == accessible.

### Functions

| [`analyze_a11y`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.a11y.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.a11y.analyze_a11y)(ctx)   | Emit a11y Findings from DOM perennials (+ axe results if captured).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.analysis.ux.a11y.analyze_a11y(ctx)

Emit a11y Findings from DOM perennials (+ axe results if captured).

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus

Contrast + focus analyzer (deterministic, no engine).

Contrast ratios are computed from the captured `a11y_styles` artifact (effective
fg/bg colors) with the exact WCAG relative-luminance formula and the 4.5:1 normal
/ 3:1 large+UI thresholds (D3 §3). Focus issues that are statically detectable
(positive `tabindex`) are flagged from the DOM; the genuinely behavioral focus
properties (keyboard traps, focus-order *logicality*, visible-focus indicator)
need active key-driving and are routed to `needs_human_review` rather than
asserted – the honesty constraint again.

### Functions

| [`analyze_contrast_focus`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.analyze_contrast_focus)(ctx)   | Emit contrast Findings + statically-detectable focus Findings.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`contrast_ratio`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.contrast_ratio)(fg, bg)        | WCAG contrast ratio between two sRGB colors (>=1.0).             |
| [`relative_luminance`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.relative_luminance)(rgb)       | WCAG relative luminance of an sRGB `(r, g, b)` in 0-255.         |

### ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.analyze_contrast_focus(ctx)

Emit contrast Findings + statically-detectable focus Findings.

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)

### ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.contrast_ratio(fg, bg)

WCAG contrast ratio between two sRGB colors (>=1.0).

```pycon
>>> contrast_ratio([0, 0, 0], [255, 255, 255])
21.0
>>> round(contrast_ratio([255, 255, 255], [255, 255, 255]), 1)
1.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.relative_luminance(rgb)

WCAG relative luminance of an sRGB `(r, g, b)` in 0-255.

```pycon
>>> relative_luminance([255, 255, 255])
1.0
>>> relative_luminance([0, 0, 0])
0.0
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.cwv.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.cwv

Core Web Vitals analyzer: performance-as-UX from the captured `perf` artifacts.

Computes INP (group `event` entries by `interactionId`, max duration; 200ms),
CLS (sum `layout-shift` values excluding `hadRecentInput`, already filtered at
capture; 0.1), and LCP/TTFB from the most complete perf snapshot. Per D3, LCP/FCP/
TTFB are **initial-load-only** until the Soft Navigations API lands, so those
findings are labelled provisional. True per-step bucketing by wall-clock window is
a depth item; here metrics are attributed at the page level.

### Functions

| [`analyze_cwv`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.cwv.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.cwv.analyze_cwv)(ctx)       | Emit performance Findings from the most complete perf snapshot.      |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cwv_from_perf`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.cwv.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.cwv.cwv_from_perf)(payload) | Reduce one perf payload to `{inp, cls, lcp, ttfb}` (pure, testable). |

### ov.analysis.ux.cwv.analyze_cwv(ctx)

Emit performance Findings from the most complete perf snapshot.

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)

### ov.analysis.ux.cwv.cwv_from_perf(payload)

Reduce one perf payload to `{inp, cls, lcp, ttfb}` (pure, testable).

```pycon
>>> cwv_from_perf({"vitals": {"inp": [{"duration": 50, "interactionId": 1},
...                                    {"duration": 90, "interactionId": 1}],
...                            "cls": [{"value": 0.05}, {"value": 0.03}],
...                            "lcp": [{"value": 1200}]},
...                 "navigation": {"ttfb": 300}})
{'inp': 90, 'cls': 0.08, 'lcp': 1200, 'ttfb': 300}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.forms.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.forms

Form-records analyzer: the state-changing actions a page offers, and what guards them (#21).

One record per `<form>` (and per AJAX submission found in inline scripts) in the captured DOM:
page URL, resolved action, method, encoding, fields, and the protections around it (CSRF token,
honeypot-like fields, captcha, file upload, navigation-only forms). From the main document’s
response headers it adds the session cookie’s `SameSite` and the framing policy. Read-only: it
only reads captured artifacts and never submits anything. Writes one `forms` artifact (a JSON
list) and a summary; it emits no findings.

Caveat: `Set-Cookie` values are redacted at capture by default (`redact_values`), so
`session_cookie_samesite` is `None` unless the run was captured with redaction off.

### Functions

| [`analyze_forms`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.forms.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.forms.analyze_forms)(ctx)              | Write a `forms` artifact (JSON list of form records) for the run's captured pages.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`extract_forms`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.forms.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.forms.extract_forms)(html[, page_url]) | Form records for every `<form>` and inline-script AJAX POST in `html` (pure).        |
| [`header_facts`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.forms.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.forms.header_facts)(headers)           | Response-header facts that decide how a site can be posted to or framed (pure).      |

### ov.analysis.ux.forms.analyze_forms(ctx)

Write a `forms` artifact (JSON list of form records) for the run’s captured pages.

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)

### ov.analysis.ux.forms.extract_forms(html, page_url='')

Form records for every `<form>` and inline-script AJAX POST in `html` (pure).

```pycon
>>> recs = extract_forms('<form action="/go" method="post"><input name="_token" type="hidden"></form>', "https://x.org/a")
>>> recs[0]["action"], recs[0]["method"], recs[0]["protections"]["csrf"]
```

  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.heuristics.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.heuristics

Heuristic analyzer: the automatable subset of Nielsen / cognitive-walkthrough (D3 §6).

Each heuristic maps to a machine-observable signal computed from the journey
trace + console + DOM:

* **console-error-on-step** – a console error emitted during a step (robustness).
* **missing feedback (Nielsen H1 / CW Q4)** – a `click` whose post-observation
  hash is unchanged with no console/network delta (no visible response).
* **live-region presence (WCAG 4.1.3)** – dynamic states but no `aria-live` /
  `role=status` region to announce them.

The Operator’s per-step *intent* is the cognitive-walkthrough ground truth for
“expected action”, so a noop on an intentful click is a meaningful signal.

### Functions

| [`analyze_heuristics`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.heuristics.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.heuristics.analyze_heuristics)(ctx)   | Emit Findings for console-on-step, missing feedback, and live-region absence.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.analysis.ux.heuristics.analyze_heuristics(ctx)

Emit Findings for console-on-step, missing feedback, and live-region absence.

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux

UX + accessibility deterministic analyzers (§5.1, D3).

Each module registers an analyzer that reads captured artifacts and emits
normalized `Finding`s with ``severity = impact_tier x reach``.
The hard honesty constraint (D3) lives here: automated tooling catches only
~30-40% of WCAG issues, so the non-automatable tail is routed to
`needs_human_review` and never asserted as resolved.

### Modules

| [`a11y`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.a11y.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.a11y)                     | Accessibility analyzer: WebAIM perennials from the DOM + optional axe mapping.               |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`contrast_focus`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus) | Contrast + focus analyzer (deterministic, no engine).                                        |
| [`cwv`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.cwv.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.cwv)                       | Core Web Vitals analyzer: performance-as-UX from the captured `perf` artifacts.              |
| [`forms`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.forms.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.forms)                   | Form-records analyzer: the state-changing actions a page offers, and what guards them (#21). |
| [`heuristics`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.heuristics.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.heuristics)         | Heuristic analyzer: the automatable subset of Nielsen / cognitive-walkthrough (D3 §6).       |
| [`metrics`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.metrics.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.metrics)               | Journey-metrics analyzer: form friction, backtracking, and journey summary (D3 §5).          |
| [`severity`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.severity)             | Severity scoring: `score = impact_tier x reach` (D3 §1).                                     |


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.metrics.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.metrics

Journey-metrics analyzer: form friction, backtracking, and journey summary (D3 §5).

Form friction is the headline finding – conversion drops sharply across the 5-7
field cliff, so forms are scored by field/required count. Backtracking and
dead-ends are read from the journey trace (revisited observation hashes, noop/
error steps). Descriptive journey metrics (steps, distinct states, success) are
surfaced in the analyzer summary for the report’s overview section.

### Functions

| [`analyze_metrics`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.metrics.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.metrics.analyze_metrics)(ctx)                       | Emit form-friction + backtracking Findings and a journey summary.        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`form_friction`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.metrics.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.metrics.form_friction)(field_count, required_count) | Map a form's field counts to (impact_tier, note) past the 5-field cliff. |

### ov.analysis.ux.metrics.analyze_metrics(ctx)

Emit form-friction + backtracking Findings and a journey summary.

* **Return type:**
  [`AnalyzerOutput`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.context.html.md#ov.analysis.context.AnalyzerOutput)

### ov.analysis.ux.metrics.form_friction(field_count, required_count)

Map a form’s field counts to (impact_tier, note) past the 5-field cliff.

```pycon
>>> form_friction(3, 2) is None
True
>>> form_friction(6, 4)[0]
'moderate'
>>> form_friction(10, 8)[0]
'critical'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md

# ov.analysis.ux.severity

Severity scoring: `score = impact_tier x reach` (D3 §1).

The design goal is that a high-reach moderate issue outranks a rare critical one.
`reach` combines how many nodes/states an issue touches with the fraction of
the journey it affects:

```default
reach_magnitude = max(nodes, states_affected, 1)
reach_value     = reach_magnitude * journey_fraction
score           = impact_weight * reach_value
```

So a *serious* (3) issue on 12 nodes across 80% of journeys scores
`3 * (12 * 0.8) = 28.8`, while a *critical* (4) issue on 1 node in 5% of
journeys scores `4 * (1 * 0.05) = 0.2` – exactly the prioritization D3 wants.

### Module Attributes

| [`A11Y_TIER_WEIGHT`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.severity.A11Y_TIER_WEIGHT)   | axe-style accessibility impact tiers -> numeric weight.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`UX_TIER_WEIGHT`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.severity.UX_TIER_WEIGHT)     | Nielsen UX severity tiers (0 cosmetic .                   |

### Functions

| [`make_severity`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.severity.make_severity)(impact_tier, \*[, nodes, ...])   | Build a [`Severity`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Severity) with the `impact x reach` score.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`tier_weight`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.severity.html.md#ov.analysis.ux.severity.tier_weight)(impact_tier)                       | Map an a11y label or a UX `"0".."4"` tier to its numeric weight (default 2).                                          |

### ov.analysis.ux.severity.UX_TIER_WEIGHT *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]* *= {'0': 0, '1': 1, '2': 2, '3': 3, '4': 4}*

# _autosummary/ov.base.html.md

# ov.base

Single source of truth (SSOT) for the `ov` artifact schema.

One Pydantic v2 model tree defines *what a capture is* and \*what an analysis
produces\*. Every other module reads from these models rather than inventing its
own shapes – this is the SSOT discipline from the build specification (§3.3).

The tree has four families:

* **Operate value types** – [`Action`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Action), [`Affordance`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Affordance),
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation), [`ActionResult`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ActionResult), [`ProgressSignal`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ProgressSignal). These
  > are the deterministic, model-free currency of the `operate/` “hands”.
* **Capture artifacts** – [`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact), [`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep),
  [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun). What a browser session records.
* **Inferred facts** – [`Scored`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Scored), [`TechFinding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.TechFinding),
  [`Endpoint`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Endpoint). Probabilistic conclusions that always carry confidence and
  > provenance (D2: outputs are never ground truth).
* **Analysis outputs** – [`Evidence`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Evidence), [`Severity`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Severity),
  [`Finding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding), [`EvidenceBundle`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.EvidenceBundle). The normalized currency of the
  > analysis lenses and the grounded LLM layer (D3 + D4).
* **Review/regression outputs** – [`FindingDelta`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta), [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff). The
  own-target *drift* between a run and a stored prior baseline (review mode,
  §10); cheap by design because artifacts are content-addressed.

## Design notes

* IDs are generated by [`new_id()`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.new_id) (prefix + short uuid) so artifacts and
  findings are addressable and joinable across the store.
* `confidence` appears twice on purpose, matching the spec: [`Scored`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Scored)
  uses an integer 0-100 (Wappalyzer-style) for *detected technologies*;
  [`Finding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding) carries a float 0-1 for *analysis judgments*.

### Functions

| [`new_id`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.new_id)([prefix])   | Return a short, unique, prefixed id, e.g. `"step_3f9a1c2b"`.         |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`utcnow`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.utcnow)()           | Timezone-aware current UTC time (the project's canonical timestamp). |

### Classes

| [`Action`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Action)(\*, type[, ref, description, text, ...])    | A single deterministic operation against the target.                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ActionResult`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ActionResult)(\*, action, ok[, error, ...])         | Outcome of `ov.operate.act.act()` -- success/error *plus* a fresh read.           |
| [`Affordance`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Affordance)(\*, ref, role[, name, bbox, ...])       | One actionable element as perceived by a perception strategy.                     |
| [`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)(\*[, artifact_id, step_id, uri, ...])     | A content-addressed blob in the store, referenced by id everywhere else.          |
| [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun)(\*[, run_id, target_url, mode, ...])    | Everything one `observe` produced; artifacts live in the store by id.             |
| [`Endpoint`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Endpoint)(\*[, confidence, provenance, kind, ...])  | One synthesized API endpoint, with GenSON-merged request/response schemas.        |
| [`Evidence`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Evidence)(\*[, evidence_id, artifact_id, ...])      | The addressable unit an LLM claim must cite (D4).                                 |
| [`EvidenceBundle`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.EvidenceBundle)(\*[, step_id, contract, ...])       | The grounded bundle a vision LLM reasons over (assembled model-free; §8.1).       |
| [`Finding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding)(\*[, finding_id, title, ...])              | SSOT for every UX / a11y / perf / arch / robustness finding (D3 + D4).            |
| [`FindingDelta`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta)(\*, key, status[, direction, ...])    | One finding's status between a run and its baseline (review-mode currency).       |
| [`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep)(\*[, id, intent, action, ...])         | One recorded step of the user journey -- doubles as UX evidence (§2.3).           |
| [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)(\*, strategy[, url, affordances, ...]) | The uniform result of any perception strategy (a pure read).                      |
| [`ProgressSignal`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ProgressSignal)(\*[, repeated_action, ...])         | Deterministic loop / no-progress *facts* (the package never decides to stop).     |
| [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff)(\*, run_id, baseline_run_id[, ...])        | Own-target regression: a run vs a stored prior baseline run (review mode, §10).   |
| [`Scored`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Scored)(\*[, confidence, provenance])               | Mixin for every inferred (non-observed) fact.                                     |

| [`TechFinding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.TechFinding)(\*[, confidence, provenance, ...])     | One detected technology (framework, library, CDN, analytics, hosting).            |

Bases: `BaseModel`

A single deterministic operation against the target.

Mirrors Playwright-MCP’s require-description-and-ref safety: actions that
touch an element carry a `ref` (a stable affordance handle) *and* a human
`description` so the journal records intent legibly.

SSOT for every UX / a11y / perf / arch / robustness finding (D3 + D4).

The hard fact/judgment split lives here: `evidence_refs` are *cited*
(never authored by a model), `judgment` is model interpretation only. A
finding with no resolvable evidence is rejected (cite-or-abstain); the
honest “can’t tell from the evidence” outcome is `type="undetermined"`.

### *class* ov.base.RunDiff(\*, run_id, baseline_run_id, target_url='', created_at=<factory>, finding_deltas=<factory>, tech_added=<factory>, tech_removed=<factory>, endpoints_added=<factory>, endpoints_removed=<factory>, rendering_model_change=None, source_maps_change=None, notes=<factory>)

Bases: `BaseModel`

Own-target regression: a run vs a stored prior baseline run (review mode, §10).

Produced by [`ov.analysis.diff.diff_runs()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.diff.html.md#ov.analysis.diff.diff_runs) from two analyzed
`CaptureRun`s of the same target. The :attr:`finding_deltas` list is
the SSOT; [`counts`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff.counts)/[`has_drift`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff.has_drift) are *derived* (`@computed_field`,
so they serialize) and [`regressions`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff.regressions)/[`improvements`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff.improvements) are views over
the deltas – nothing is stored twice.

```pycon
>>> d = RunDiff(run_id="run_b", baseline_run_id="run_a", finding_deltas=[
...     FindingDelta(key="k1", status="new", direction="regression"),
...     FindingDelta(key="k2", status="resolved", direction="improvement"),
... ])
>>> d.counts["new"], d.counts["resolved"], d.has_drift
(1, 1, True)
>>> [r.key for r in d.regressions], [i.key for i in d.improvements]
(['k1'], ['k2'])
```

#### *property* counts *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*

Per-status tallies derived from the deltas (the headline of a diff).

#### *property* has_drift *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

`True` if anything changed across runs (findings, stack, API, or model).

#### *property* improvements *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[FindingDelta](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta)]*

Deltas that were resolved or got better since the baseline.

#### model_config *: [ClassVar](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.ClassVar)[ConfigDict]* *= {}*

Configuration for the model, should be a dictionary conforming to [`ConfigDict`][pydantic.config.ConfigDict].

#### *property* regressions *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[FindingDelta](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta)]*

Deltas that got worse or are newly present (a downstream fix list).

# _autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md

# ov.capture.browser

Playwright facade – the baseline driver (§9, D1).

This hides Playwright behind a clean lifecycle so no caller (or skill, or future
agent) ever touches a raw Playwright object. It is treated as a \*facade over a
CDP escape hatch, not a wall\*: [`BrowserSession.cdp()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession.cdp) lazily attaches a
[`CdpSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md#ov.capture.cdp.CdpSession) for the ~20% the high-level API can’t reach.

The sync Playwright API is used deliberately – capture is a synchronous,
step-by-step orchestration and the sync API keeps the code legible. HAR is
recorded to a temp `.har.zip` with embedded bodies and read back after the
context closes (HAR only flushes on `context.close()`); structured network
records come from event accumulation in the network probe, not from the HAR.

### Classes

| [`BrowserSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession)(config, \*[, record_har])   | Owns a Playwright browser/context/page for one capture run.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`BrowserNotAvailable`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserNotAvailable)   | Raised when Playwright or its browsers are not usable.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|

### *exception* ov.capture.browser.BrowserNotAvailable

Bases: [`RuntimeError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#RuntimeError)

Raised when Playwright or its browsers are not usable.

Carries the install hint so the message is actionable, per the project’s
informative-errors principle.

### *class* ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession(config, , record_har=True)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Owns a Playwright browser/context/page for one capture run.

Lifecycle is explicit ([`start()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession.start) / [`close()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession.close)) so the orchestrator can
flush in-memory probe state *before* closing the context (which flushes HAR),
then ingest the HAR. It is also a context manager for simple call sites.

#### cdp()

Lazily attach and return a [`CdpSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md#ov.capture.cdp.CdpSession) (Chromium).

Returns `None` on non-Chromium browsers, where CDP is unavailable.

#### close()

Close the context (flushing HAR), read the HAR, then tear down.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### *property* context

The active Playwright `BrowserContext`.

#### *property* har_bytes *: [bytes](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)*

The recorded HAR archive bytes (available only after [`close()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession.close)).

#### *property* page

The active Playwright `Page` (raises if not started).

#### start()

Launch the browser and open a context + page. Returns self.

* **Return type:**
  [`BrowserSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.browser.html.md#ov.capture.browser.BrowserSession)

#### stop()

Hard teardown of browser + playwright (idempotent).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md

# ov.capture.cdp

The CDP escape-hatch plugin (Chromium-only) – the ~20% Playwright can’t reach.

Per D1, attach a CDP session to the same page and use it for: the full
accessibility tree (`Accessibility.getFullAXTree`), Server-Sent-Event frames
(`Network.eventSourceMessageReceived`, which `page.route` cannot reliably
intercept), runtime counters (`Performance.getMetrics`), and the TLS
certificate. `response.body()` eviction recovery via `Network.getResponseBody`
is also exposed but not relied on by the default network probe.

Critical gotcha encoded here: in an AX node, `role`/`name`/`value` are
`AXValue` *objects*, so the accessible name lives at `node["name"]["value"]`;
and `getFullAXTree` does **not** cross-origin-recurse, so frames are handled
one at a time. CDP is Chromium-only – an accepted constraint for the capture tail.

### Functions

| [`flatten_ax_node`](_autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md#ov.capture.cdp.flatten_ax_node)(node)   | Flatten a raw CDP AX node into `{role, name, value, ...}` plain values.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`CdpSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md#ov.capture.cdp.CdpSession)(client)   | A thin, friendly wrapper over a Playwright `CDPSession` (Chromium).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A thin, friendly wrapper over a Playwright `CDPSession` (Chromium).

#### capture_sse(sink)

Append every SSE frame to `sink` (`Network.eventSourceMessageReceived`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### enable_network()

Enable the `Network` domain once (required for SSE + body recovery).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### get_certificate(origin)

Return the TLS certificate info for `origin` (`Network.getCertificate`).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

`getFullAXTree` does not recurse cross-origin frames; pass `frame_id`

# ov.capture

Capture layer: drive a browser and record behavioral + static streams.

The public entry point is [`CaptureSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.session.html.md#ov.capture.session.CaptureSession); persisted
state lives in [`CaptureStore`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore). Probes are registered
plugins (see [`ov.capture.probes`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#module-ov.capture.probes)).

### Modules

|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`cdp`](_autosummary/ov.capture.cdp.html.md#module-ov.capture.cdp)           | The CDP escape-hatch plugin (Chromium-only) -- the ~20% Playwright can't reach. |
| [`probes`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#module-ov.capture.probes)     | Probes -- the registerable units of *what intelligence to gather* (§2).         |
| [`session`](_autosummary/ov.capture.session.html.md#module-ov.capture.session)   | `CaptureSession` -- owns the browser and orchestrates the probes (§3.1).        |
| [`stores`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#module-ov.capture.stores)     | The capture store -- a `MutableMapping` Mall over a run directory (§3.4).       |


# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.a11y.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.a11y

Accessibility-signals probe: computed text styles (for contrast) + optional axe.

Contrast cannot be judged from static DOM – it needs *computed* colors. This
probe snapshots, per visible text element, the effective foreground/background
colors, font size/weight, and bbox, so the deterministic
[`ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus.html.md#module-ov.analysis.ux.contrast_focus) analyzer can compute WCAG ratios offline.

If an axe-core bundle is resolvable (`OV_AXE_PATH` or the sidecar’s
`node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js`), it is injected and `axe.run()` results
are stored as an `axe` artifact – additive, never required. axe-core is used
as an external tool here (no vendoring), keeping the package license-clean.

### Classes

| [`A11yProbe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.a11y.html.md#ov.capture.probes.a11y.A11yProbe)()   | Capture computed text styles (always) + axe-core results (when available).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.capture.probes.a11y.A11yProbe

Bases: [`Probe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe)

Capture computed text styles (always) + axe-core results (when available).

#### capture(ctx)

Snapshot current state into artifacts. Default: nothing.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)]

# ov.capture.probes.assets

Assets probe: a content-addressed inventory of loaded resources.

Bodies are already stored by the `network` probe (content-addressed, so they
dedupe). This probe builds the *inventory*: one manifest row per resource with
url, MIME, size, hash, and the body artifact id when captured. It `requires`
the network stream and therefore runs after it (registry ordering).

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.dom.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.dom

DOM probe: serialized DOM + ARIA snapshot (agent view) + full AX tree (evidence).

Two accessibility views, per the progressive-disclosure rule (§9): the concise
**ARIA snapshot** (`locator.aria_snapshot` – ~200-400 tokens, the agent’s
view) and the full CDP **AX tree** (recorded as evidence). The serialized DOM
(`page.content()`) is stored for the rendering-model diff and selector lookups.
Runs per captured state so SPA/modal/revealed-menu states are each recorded.

### Classes

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.fingerprint

Fingerprint probe: a built-in, license-clean technology detector.

The spec flags `wappalyzer-next` and the `enthec/webappanalyzer` ruleset as
GPL-3.0, incompatible with `ov`’s MIT license (§6.2). So rather than depend on
them, this probe ships a small deterministic detector over the highest-signal,
lowest-false-positive sources: framework state-injection globals
(`__NEXT_DATA__`/`__NUXT__`/`__remixContext` …), devtools hooks, bundler
signatures, the `<meta name=generator>` tag, `ng-version`, and response
headers. `wappalyzer`/Retire.js remain available as *optional* external CLIs.

Each detection is a [`TechFinding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.TechFinding) carrying confidence + provenance
and is appended to `ctx.run.fingerprint` so `ov observe` populates the run
immediately; the raw signals are also stored as an artifact for re-analysis.

### Functions

| [`detect_technologies`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.html.md#ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.detect_technologies)(signals[, headers])   | Map captured fingerprint signals (+ headers) into scored :class:<br/><br/>```<br/>`<br/>```<br/><br/>TechFinding\`s.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`FingerprintProbe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.html.md#ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.FingerprintProbe)()   | Gather in-page signals + headers and populate `run.fingerprint`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.FingerprintProbe

Bases: [`Probe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe)

Gather in-page signals + headers and populate `run.fingerprint`.

#### finalize(ctx)

Flush accumulated state into artifacts at run end. Default: nothing.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)]

### ov.capture.probes.fingerprint.detect_technologies(signals, headers=None)

Map captured fingerprint signals (+ headers) into scored :class:

```
`
```

TechFinding\`s.

Reusable across modules (the arch analyzer enriches these with bundle/source
-map evidence). Prefers `js`/`dom` signals over loose header regex.

```pycon
>>> findings = detect_technologies({"globals": {"__NEXT_DATA__": True}})
>>> sorted(f.name for f in findings)
['Next.js', 'React']
```

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md

# ov.capture.probes

Probes – the registerable units of *what intelligence to gather* (§2).

Each probe is an independent plugin that writes typed artifacts into the capture
store. A probe is a small class implementing the [`Probe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe) lifecycle:

* [`Probe.attach()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe.attach) – subscribe event listeners *before* navigation (used by
  the streaming probes: network, console, navigation, websocket, sse).
* [`Probe.capture()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe.capture) – snapshot the current state into artifacts (used by the
  per-state probes: dom, screenshot, perf, storage, fingerprint).
* [`Probe.finalize()`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe.finalize) – flush accumulated state into artifacts at run end.

Probes are registered with `register_probe()` and ordered by the registry’s
`requires`/`produces` dependency declarations, so e.g. `assets` (which
needs the network stream) runs after `network`.

### Functions

| [`load_builtin_probes`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.load_builtin_probes)()   | Import the builtin probe modules so their `@register_probe` runs.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Probe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe)()                                       | Base class for probes; override only the lifecycle hooks you need.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ProbeContext`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.ProbeContext)(store, run, config[, page, ...]) | Everything a probe needs, injected by the `CaptureSession`.          |

### *class* ov.capture.probes.Probe

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Base class for probes; override only the lifecycle hooks you need.

#### attach(ctx)

Subscribe listeners before navigation. Default: no-op.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### capture(ctx)

Snapshot current state into artifacts. Default: nothing.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)]

#### finalize(ctx)

Flush accumulated state into artifacts at run end. Default: nothing.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)]

### *class* ov.capture.probes.ProbeContext(store, run, config, page=None, cdp=None, step=None, extras=dict())

Everything a probe needs, injected by the `CaptureSession`.

`extras` is shared scratch (e.g. the accumulating network record list) so

### ov.capture.probes.load_builtin_probes()

Import the builtin probe modules so their `@register_probe` runs.

Safe to call repeatedly (imports are cached). It is also invoked once at the
bottom of this module so that simply importing [`ov.capture.probes`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#module-ov.capture.probes)
yields a fully-populated `PROBE_REGISTRY` – no caller (the session, a
test, a skill) ever observes a half-registered registry depending on import
order. The probe modules pull in no heavy/browser dependencies at import.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.navigation.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.navigation

Navigation probe: URL changes, redirects, frame tree, and SPA history.

Hard navigations are captured from `framenavigated`; SPA soft navigations
(`history.pushState`/`replaceState`/`popstate`) are captured by injecting a
tiny init script that records URL changes onto `window.__ov_nav` and reading it
back at finalize. This keeps client-side route changes visible even when no
network request accompanies them.

### Classes

| [`NavigationProbe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.navigation.html.md#ov.capture.probes.navigation.NavigationProbe)()   | Record hard navigations (events) + soft SPA navigations (injected hook).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Record hard navigations (events) + soft SPA navigations (injected hook).

#### attach(ctx)

Subscribe listeners before navigation. Default: no-op.

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.network.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.network

Network probe: request/response metadata + bodies, accumulated from events.

Structured records come from Playwright `request`/`response` events (which we
control), not from the HAR file – the HAR is stored separately by the session as
a raw artifact. Bodies are captured only for configured content types and under
the size cap; `response.body()` eviction is caught and recorded as a fact
rather than crashing the run (D1: design around eviction from day one).

Headers are redacted by default (privacy): cookie/auth/token headers never
persist as raw values unless `config.capture_secrets` is set.

### Classes

| [`NetworkProbe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.network.html.md#ov.capture.probes.network.NetworkProbe)()   | Accumulate request/response records (+ size-capped bodies) via events.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.capture.probes.network.NetworkProbe

Bases: [`Probe`](_autosummary/ov.capture.probes.html.md#ov.capture.probes.Probe)

Accumulate request/response records (+ size-capped bodies) via events.

Subscribe listeners before navigation. Default: no-op.

  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.perf.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.perf

Performance probe: Navigation Timing, paint, web-vitals entries, CDP counters.

An init script installs `PerformanceObserver``s that accumulate layout-shift and
event-timing entries onto ``window.__ov_perf` (so per-step CWV attribution is
possible downstream); at each captured state the probe reads those plus the
Navigation Timing and paint entries, and – on Chromium – `Performance.getMetrics`
via CDP. Web-vitals *attribution* (naming the offending element) is refined in the
`cwv` analyzer; this probe captures the raw entries deterministically.

|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.sse.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.sse

SSE probe: Server-Sent-Event frames via CDP (Chromium-only).

SSE frames are *not* reliably reachable through `page.route` or
`response.body()`, so this probe uses `Network.eventSourceMessageReceived`
through the CDP escape hatch (which requires `Network.enable`). When CDP is
unavailable (non-Chromium), the probe is inert.

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.storage.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.storage

Storage probe: cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB names.

Values are **redacted by default** (privacy; `config.redact_values`) – we keep
the *shape* of client state (which keys exist, how big) without persisting
secrets/PII. sessionStorage is read manually (it is not in `storage_state`) and
IndexedDB is probed for database names only (deep dumps are fragile and deferred).

# _autosummary/ov.capture.probes.websocket.html.md

# ov.capture.probes.websocket

WebSocket probe: frames sent/received and open/close, first-class (D1).

Uses `page.on("websocket")` -> `framesent`/`framereceived`/`close` (a
high-level Playwright API, *not* CDP). Frame payloads are truncated to a sane cap
to keep the store bounded; realtime *shape* synthesis happens later in arch
analysis, not here.

# _autosummary/ov.capture.session.html.md

# ov.capture.session

`CaptureSession` – owns the browser and orchestrates the probes (§3.1).

The session is the deterministic capture spine: it resolves and dependency-orders
the enabled probes, attaches their listeners before navigation, snapshots state
on demand (the `snapshot_state` primitive of §2.3), finalizes and flushes them
at the end, stores the HAR, and persists the [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun).

It exposes `page` so the `operate` primitives and the scripted driver can act
on the same browser, and is a context manager for safe teardown.

### Classes

| [`CaptureSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.session.html.md#ov.capture.session.CaptureSession)(\*, target_url[, config, ...])   | Drive one target and record everything into the store (zero-config default).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.capture.session.CaptureSession(, target_url, config=None, store=None, mode='reconstruct', probes='default', record_har=True, read_only=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Drive one target and record everything into the store (zero-config default).

Typical use is via the [`ov.observe()`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.observe) facade, but the session is directly
usable:

```default
with CaptureSession(target_url="https://example.com") as s:
    s.open()                 # navigate to target_url + capture the load state
    run = s.run
```

#### capture_step(step)

#### *property* page

The active Playwright `Page` for `operate` primitives / the driver.

# _autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md

# ov.capture.stores

The capture store – a `MutableMapping` Mall over a run directory (§3.4).

A single root holds many runs. Artifacts are **content-addressed** (keyed by a
hash of their bytes) so identical assets dedupe across runs – which is exactly
what makes own-target diffing cheap. `dol` provides the filesystem-backed
mappings; this module is a thin facade that adds the `ov` semantics (typed
runs, artifact put/get, report + analysis storage) on top.

Layout under `root`:

```default
runs/<run_id>.json          # CaptureRun, JSON
artifacts/<hash>.<ext>      # content-addressed bytes (shared across runs)
reports/<run_id>/<name>     # rendered Markdown
analyses/<analysis_id>.json # analysis JSON
```

The Mall exposes four `MutableMapping` attributes (`runs`, `artifacts`,
`reports`, `analyses`) for callers who want raw access, plus convenience
methods that speak the SSOT models.

### Functions

| [`resolve_store`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.resolve_store)(store)   | Coerce `store` (a CaptureStore, a path, or `None`) into a CaptureStore.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`CaptureStore`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore)([root])   | A store of stores for one or many capture runs (XDG-aligned root by default).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore(root=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A store of stores for one or many capture runs (XDG-aligned root by default).

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> store = CaptureStore(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> art = store.put_artifact(b"<html>hi</html>", kind="dom")
>>> store.artifact_bytes(art) == b"<html>hi</html>"
True
>>> from ov.base import CaptureRun
>>> run = CaptureRun(target_url="http://x", artifacts=[art])
>>> store.save_run(run)
>>> store.load_run(run.run_id).target_url
'http://x'
```

#### artifact_bytes(artifact_or_uri)

Return the raw bytes for an `Artifact` (or a raw `uri` string).

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

#### load_analysis(analysis_id)

Load an analysis JSON blob by id.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

#### load_run(run_id)

Load a `CaptureRun` by id (accepts bare id or `<id>.json`).

* **Return type:**
  [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun)

#### put_artifact(data, , kind, step_id=None, content_type=None, meta=None)

Store `data` content-addressed and return its `Artifact` record.

Identical bytes produce the same `uri`, so re-storing is a no-op write
and cross-run assets dedupe automatically.

* **Return type:**
  [`Artifact`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Artifact)

#### report_names(run_id)

List report keys belonging to `run_id` (separator-normalized).

`dol` returns directory-listing keys with the OS separator, which is a
backslash on Windows; we always speak the logical `/` separator (and
store/read with it), so normalize before the prefix match.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### run_ids()

List stored run ids (without the `.json` suffix).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### save_analysis(analysis_id, obj)

Persist an analysis JSON blob by id.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### save_report(run_id, name, markdown)

Store a rendered Markdown report; return its store key.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### save_run(run)

Persist a `CaptureRun` as JSON under its `run_id`.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### ov.capture.stores.resolve_store(store)

Coerce `store` (a CaptureStore, a path, or `None`) into a CaptureStore.

The dependency-injection seam: callers pass whatever they have and get a
usable store, defaulting to the XDG root.

* **Return type:**
  [`CaptureStore`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore)


# _autosummary/ov.config.html.md

# ov.config

Configuration – the single source of truth for `ov`’s defaults.

Everything is a keyword-only field on [`OvConfig`](_autosummary/ov.config.html.md#ov.config.OvConfig) with a smart default, so
`ov.observe(url)` works with zero config while every knob stays reachable.
Environment variables (`OV_*`) override the defaults; an explicit constructor
argument overrides the environment.

This module also encodes the **default-safety checklist** from the spec’s
boundary note (§6): redaction is on, secret/PII capture is off, a polite rate is
applied, `robots.txt` intent is respected by default, and a *foreign* target
requires an explicit `authorized=True` acknowledgement.

### Functions

| [`default_store_root`](_autosummary/ov.config.html.md#ov.config.default_store_root)()   | Return the XDG-aligned default root for `ov`'s capture stores.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`OvConfig`](_autosummary/ov.config.html.md#ov.config.OvConfig)(\*[, store_root, headed, browser, ...])   | Resolved settings for a capture/analysis run (keyword-only, env-overridable).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* ov.config.OvConfig(, store_root=default_store_root(), headed=False, browser='chromium', nav_timeout_ms=30000, default_probes=('navigation', 'network', 'dom', 'screenshot', 'console', 'fingerprint', 'assets', 'a11y'), max_body_bytes=2000000, console_text_cap=2000, ws_frame_cap=4096, capture_body_content_types=('application/json', 'application/javascript', 'text/javascript', 'text/html', 'text/css', 'text/event-stream', 'application/graphql', 'application/xml', 'text/plain'), max_steps=40, max_failures=6, wall_clock_s=300.0, no_progress_steps=3, redact_values=True, capture_secrets=False, respect_robots=True, polite_rate_s=0.3, authorized=False, use_proxy=False, stealth_profile=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

# _autosummary/ov.html.md

# ov

`ov` – OverView: agent-driven web reconnaissance & analysis.

Point `ov` at a URL and it drives the target like a user, recording two
parallel streams – the *behavioral* stream (what the app does) and the *static*
stream (what it is made of) – then runs two analysis lenses (UX and
software-design) and renders Markdown reports plus a single synopsis.

This module is the **progressive-disclosure facade**: the five top-level
functions below are all most callers need, and each works with sensible defaults.
Everything underneath (capture probes, operate primitives, analyzers, report
sections) is reachable but never required.

```pycon
>>> import ov
>>> callable(ov.observe) and callable(ov.overview)
True
```

The primary consumption model is a *host agent* (Claude Code) wielding these
functions via the skills in `.claude/skills/` – the deterministic core here
runs with no model and no host.

### Functions

| [`observe`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.observe)(url, \*[, goal, journey, mode, ...])   | Drive the target and capture everything.                                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`analyze`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.analyze)(run, \*[, lenses, llm, store])         | Run the deterministic UX + architecture analyzers over a captured run.      |
| [`diff`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.diff)(run, \*[, baseline, store])               | Diff an analyzed run against a prior baseline run (own-target review mode). |
| [`report`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.report)(run_or_analyses, \*[, sections, ...])   | Render Markdown reports from analyses.                                      |
| [`synopsis`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.synopsis)(reports_or_dir, \*[, out, store])     | Extract-and-aggregate many reports into one synopsis for downstream agents. |
| [`overview`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.overview)(url, \*\*kw)                          | `observe -> analyze -> report -> synopsis`, the one-liner.                  |
| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.check_requirements)(\*[, components, verbose])  | Detect missing system dependencies and print exact install commands.        |

### Classes

| [`OvConfig`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.OvConfig)(\*[, store_root, headed, browser, ...])   | Resolved settings for a capture/analysis run (keyword-only, env-overridable).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.CaptureRun)(\*[, run_id, target_url, mode, ...])    | Everything one `observe` produced; artifacts live in the store by id.           |
| [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.RunDiff)(\*, run_id, baseline_run_id[, ...])        | Own-target regression: a run vs a stored prior baseline run (review mode, §10). |
