Produced by [`ov.analysis.diff.diff_runs()`](_autosummary/ov.analysis.diff.html.md#ov.analysis.diff.diff_runs) from two analyzed
`CaptureRun`s of the same target. The :attr:`finding_deltas` list is
the SSOT; [`counts`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.RunDiff.counts)/[`has_drift`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.RunDiff.has_drift) are *derived* (`@computed_field`,
so they serialize) and [`regressions`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.RunDiff.regressions)/[`improvements`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.RunDiff.improvements) are views over
the deltas – nothing is stored twice.

```pycon
>>> d = RunDiff(run_id="run_b", baseline_run_id="run_a", finding_deltas=[
...     FindingDelta(key="k1", status="new", direction="regression"),
...     FindingDelta(key="k2", status="resolved", direction="improvement"),
... ])
>>> d.counts["new"], d.counts["resolved"], d.has_drift
(1, 1, True)
>>> [r.key for r in d.regressions], [i.key for i in d.improvements]
(['k1'], ['k2'])
```

#### *property* counts *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*

Per-status tallies derived from the deltas (the headline of a diff).

#### *property* has_drift *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

`True` if anything changed across runs (findings, stack, API, or model).

#### *property* improvements *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[FindingDelta](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta)]*

Deltas that were resolved or got better since the baseline.

#### model_config *: [ClassVar](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.ClassVar)[ConfigDict]* *= {}*

Configuration for the model, should be a dictionary conforming to [`ConfigDict`][pydantic.config.ConfigDict].

#### *property* regressions *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[FindingDelta](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.FindingDelta)]*

Deltas that got worse or are newly present (a downstream fix list).

### ov.analyze(run, , lenses=('ux', 'arch'), llm=None, store=None)

Run the deterministic UX + architecture analyzers over a captured run.

Runs fully without a model (`llm=None` is the default and the only path
needed in Phases 1-2). The host agent reasons over the returned analyses +
evidence bundle to add narrative judgment.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ov.check_requirements(, components=None, verbose=True)

Detect missing system dependencies and print exact install commands.

`components` filters which groups to check (`"browser"`, `"node"`,
`"sidecar"`, `"clis"`); `None` checks all. The deterministic analysis
core needs none of these – they gate *capture* and the *arch sidecar*, so
every requirement here is reported as optional unless capture is requested.

```pycon
>>> rep = check_requirements(components=["clis"], verbose=False)
>>> isinstance(rep, RequirementReport)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`RequirementReport`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.RequirementReport)

### ov.diff(run, , baseline=None, store=None)

Diff an analyzed run against a prior baseline run (own-target review mode).

The distinguishing capability of `mode="review"`: report what is *new*,
*changed*, or *resolved* versus a stored prior run of the same target
(regression/drift detection, §10). Fully deterministic – no browser, no model.

* **Parameters:**
  * **run** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – an analyzed [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun) or a run id.
  * **baseline** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a run/run-id to compare against, or `None` to auto-discover the
    latest prior run of the same target.
  * **store** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a [`CaptureStore`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore), a path, or `None`.
* **Return type:**
  [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
* **Returns:**
  A [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff), or `None` if no baseline exists yet (the
  first review run). Sets `Finding.diff_status` on the run in place and
  persists a `diff_<run_id>` blob that the review report + synopsis read.

### ov.observe(url, , goal=None, journey=None, mode='reconstruct', probes='default', headed=False, store=None, crawl_pages=None, config=None, authorized=None, read_only=False)

Drive the target and capture everything. Zero-config default works.

* **Parameters:**
  * **url** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the target to study.
  * **goal** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – a natural-language objective (goal-pursuit is *host* policy; the
    deterministic core records it and does the baseline journey).
  * **journey** ([`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an optional scripted action list (guided-replay), each item an
    [`Action`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Action) or a dict like `{"type": "click", "ref": "e3"}`.
  * **mode** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – `"reconstruct"` (foreign target) or `"review"` (own target).
  * **probes** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – `"default"`, `"all"`, or an iterable of probe names.
  * **headed** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – run the browser headed (default headless).
  * **store** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – a [`CaptureStore`](_autosummary/ov.capture.stores.html.md#ov.capture.stores.CaptureStore), a path, or `None`.
  * **crawl_pages** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – if set (>1), politely crawl that many same-origin pages.
  * **config** ([`OvConfig`](_autosummary/ov.config.html.md#ov.config.OvConfig) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an explicit [`OvConfig`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.OvConfig) (overrides `headed`).
  * **authorized** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – acknowledge authorization to study a *foreign* target.
  * **read_only** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – abort every non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request in the browser (pages
    that POST on load send nothing); the aborted ones are listed in a
    `blocked_requests` artifact and a run note.
* **Return type:**
  [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun)
* **Returns:**
  The populated [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun) (also persisted to the store).

### ov.overview(url, \*\*kw)

`observe -> analyze -> report -> synopsis`, the one-liner.

Returns the synopsis path/handle. This is the pit-of-success entry point.

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md

# ov.operate.driver

The scripted/guided driver – model-free journey execution (Phase 1).

Two deterministic strategies that compose the operate primitives over a
[`CaptureSession`](_autosummary/ov.capture.session.html.md#ov.capture.session.CaptureSession):

* [`replay()`](_autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md#ov.operate.driver.replay) – execute a scripted list of actions (guided-replay), capturing
  state and journaling each step.
* [`crawl()`](_autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md#ov.operate.driver.crawl) – a polite, same-origin breadth-first crawl (crawl-and-map),
  capturing each visited page and stopping on `max_pages` / no-progress.

These let the capture spine produce a real multi-state journey with **no model**.
Goal-pursuit (`advance` toward a success predicate) is the host’s job via the
`ov-operate` skill; the package supplies the hands, not the policy.

### Functions

| [`crawl`](_autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md#ov.operate.driver.crawl)(session, \*[, max_pages])   | Politely crawl same-origin links breadth-first, capturing each page.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`replay`](_autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md#ov.operate.driver.replay)(session, actions)          | Execute a scripted action list, capturing + journaling each step.      |

### ov.operate.driver.crawl(session, , max_pages=5)

Politely crawl same-origin links breadth-first, capturing each page.

Stops at `max_pages`, on `max_steps`, or when the deterministic progress
signal reports a loop. The host can run a richer crawl; this is the model-free
baseline that yields a multi-state capture.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep)]

### ov.operate.driver.replay(session, actions)

Execute a scripted action list, capturing + journaling each step.

```pycon
>>> # actions are Action models or dicts: {"type": "click", "ref": "e3"}
>>> callable(replay)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep)]


# _autosummary/ov.operate.html.md

# ov.operate

The operate layer – deterministic, LLM-free tool primitives (the “hands”).

This is the package-owned *tool plane* from §2.3. It composes as
`journal(progress(act(observe())))` and contains no model and no policy: it
perceives affordances, executes actions, records the journey, and reports
loop/no-progress *facts*. The decision of *what to do next* and *when to stop*
belongs to the policy plane – the host (Claude Code) via the `ov-operate`
skill, or, later, an in-package agent.

Primitives (each is individually callable and testable):

* `observe()` – `observe(page, strategy) -> Observation`
* `act()` – `act(page, action) -> ActionResult` (returns a fresh Observation)
* `journal()` – append a structured per-step record
* `progress()` – loop/no-progress facts (never decides to stop)
* perception strategies – [`PERCEPTION_REGISTRY`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.PERCEPTION_REGISTRY)

### Functions

| [`observe`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.observe)(page[, strategy])                          | Perceive the current page state with `strategy` and return an Observation.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`act`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.act)(page, action, \*[, perception, polite_rate_s]) | Execute `action` against `page` and return the result + a fresh Observation. |
| [`journal`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.journal)(run, step)                                 | Append `step` to `run.steps` and return it.                                  |
| [`make_step`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.make_step)(\*, intent[, action, ...])               | Build a `JourneyStep` from an action's before/after observations.            |
| [`progress`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.progress)(history, \*[, no_progress_steps])         | Compute loop/no-progress facts from the journey `history` so far.            |
| [`perceive`](_autosummary/ov.operate.html.md#ov.operate.perceive)(page[, strategy])                         | Dispatch to the named perception strategy (defaults to `ax_snapshot`).       |

### ov.operate.act(page, action, , perception='ax_snapshot', polite_rate_s=0.0)

Execute `action` against `page` and return the result + a fresh Observation.

On failure, `ok=False` and `error` carries the message; a fresh
Observation is still attached so the host can recover (re-observe, scroll,
disambiguate).

* **Return type:**
  [`ActionResult`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ActionResult)

### ov.operate.journal(run, step)

Append `step` to `run.steps` and return it.

* **Return type:**
  [`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep)

### ov.operate.make_step(, intent, action=None, pre_observation=None, result=None, artifact_ids=None, network_delta=0, console_delta=0, note=None)

Build a `JourneyStep` from an action’s before/after observations.

`outcome` is derived: `error` on a failed action, `noop` when the
post-observation hash equals the pre-observation hash (nothing changed),
else `ok`.

* **Return type:**
  [`JourneyStep`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.JourneyStep)

### ov.operate.observe(page, strategy='ax_snapshot')

Perceive the current page state with `strategy` and return an Observation.

```pycon
>>> from ov.operate.perception import PERCEPTION_REGISTRY
>>> "ax_snapshot" in PERCEPTION_REGISTRY
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)

### ov.operate.perceive(page, strategy='ax_snapshot')

Dispatch to the named perception strategy (defaults to `ax_snapshot`).

Raises `KeyError` with the known strategies when `strategy` is unknown –
an informative error per the project’s principles.

* **Return type:**
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)

### ov.operate.progress(history, , no_progress_steps=3)

Compute loop/no-progress facts from the journey `history` so far.

```pycon
>>> from ov.base import JourneyStep, Action
>>> s = JourneyStep(action=Action(type='click', ref='e1'), post_obs_hash='h')
>>> sig = progress([s, s.model_copy(), s.model_copy()], no_progress_steps=3)
>>> sig.no_new_signal_steps >= 3 and sig.loop_suspected
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`ProgressSignal`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.ProgressSignal)

### Modules

| [`driver`](_autosummary/ov.operate.driver.html.md#module-ov.operate.driver)         | The scripted/guided driver -- model-free journey execution (Phase 1).         |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`perception`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#module-ov.operate.perception) | Perception strategies -- pluggable ways to turn a page into an `Observation`. |
| [`strategies`](_autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md#module-ov.operate.strategies) | Journey-strategy helpers -- intent shaping for the three strategies (§2.3).   |


# _autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md

# ov.operate.perception

Perception strategies – pluggable ways to turn a page into an `Observation`.

A perception strategy returns a uniform [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation) so the rest
of the operate layer (and the host’s policy) stays declarative about *what* an
observation is, not *how* it was grounded. Three strategies ship:

* `ax_snapshot` – affordances from an accessibility-relevant DOM walk plus the
  concise ARIA snapshot text (cheap, deterministic, the default).
* `screenshot` – the same affordances with bounding boxes, intended to pair
  with a screenshot artifact (for canvas/exotic renderers).
* `hybrid` – AX-grounded affordances, robust when the AX layer is thin.

Affordances are extracted by stamping a stable `data-ov-ref` attribute on each
interactive element, so `act()` can target it deterministically
(`getByRole`-stable, survives CSS churn) – the require-description-and-ref
safety pattern from Playwright-MCP.

### Module Attributes

| [`REF_ATTR`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.REF_ATTR)            | The attribute stamped on interactive elements to create stable refs.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PERCEPTION_REGISTRY`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.PERCEPTION_REGISTRY) | name -> `perceiver(page) -> Observation`                               |

### Functions

| [`perceive`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.perceive)(page[, strategy])   | Dispatch to the named perception strategy (defaults to `ax_snapshot`).       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`perceive_ax_snapshot`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.perceive_ax_snapshot)(page)   | Affordances + concise ARIA snapshot text (the cheap, deterministic default). |
| [`perceive_hybrid`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.perceive_hybrid)(page)        | AX-grounded affordances + ARIA snapshot; the robust default when AX is thin. |
| [`perceive_screenshot`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.perceive_screenshot)(page)    | Affordances with bounding boxes (pairs with a screenshot artifact).          |
| [`register_perception`](_autosummary/ov.operate.perception.html.md#ov.operate.perception.register_perception)(name)    | Decorator registering a perceiver under `name`.                              |

### ov.operate.perception.PERCEPTION_REGISTRY *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [Observation](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)]]* *= {'ax_snapshot': <function perceive_ax_snapshot>, 'hybrid': <function perceive_hybrid>, 'screenshot': <function perceive_screenshot>}*

name -> `perceiver(page) -> Observation`

### ov.operate.perception.REF_ATTR *= 'data-ov-ref'*

The attribute stamped on interactive elements to create stable refs.

### ov.operate.perception.perceive(page, strategy='ax_snapshot')

Dispatch to the named perception strategy (defaults to `ax_snapshot`).

Raises `KeyError` with the known strategies when `strategy` is unknown –
an informative error per the project’s principles.

* **Return type:**
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)

### ov.operate.perception.perceive_ax_snapshot(page)

Affordances + concise ARIA snapshot text (the cheap, deterministic default).

* **Return type:**
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)

### ov.operate.perception.perceive_hybrid(page)

AX-grounded affordances + ARIA snapshot; the robust default when AX is thin.

* **Return type:**
  [`Observation`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Observation)

### ov.operate.perception.perceive_screenshot(page)

# _autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md

# ov.operate.strategies

Journey-strategy helpers – intent shaping for the three strategies (§2.3).

The three strategies reuse the same primitives, varying only the *intent* written
to the journal: crawl-and-map (`enumerate`), goal-pursuit (`advance`), and
guided-replay (`replay`). These helpers keep that vocabulary in one place and
provide the deterministic target-selection a model-free driver needs.

### Module Attributes

| [`NAV_ROLES`](_autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md#ov.operate.strategies.NAV_ROLES)   | Roles treated as navigable for crawl-and-map.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`absolutize`](_autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md#ov.operate.strategies.absolutize)(href, base_url)         | Resolve `href` against `base_url` (drops fragments).                        |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_same_origin`](_autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md#ov.operate.strategies.is_same_origin)(url, base_url)      | True when `url` shares scheme+host(+port) with `base_url`.                  |
| [`navigable_affordances`](_autosummary/ov.operate.strategies.html.md#ov.operate.strategies.navigable_affordances)(observation) | Return affordances suitable for breadth-first crawl (links/tabs/menuitems). |

### ov.operate.strategies.NAV_ROLES *= frozenset({'a', 'link', 'menuitem', 'tab'})*

Roles treated as navigable for crawl-and-map.

### ov.operate.strategies.absolutize(href, base_url)

Resolve `href` against `base_url` (drops fragments).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ov.operate.strategies.is_same_origin(url, base_url)

True when `url` shares scheme+host(+port) with `base_url`.

```pycon
>>> is_same_origin("https://x.com/a", "https://x.com/b")
True
>>> is_same_origin("https://y.com/a", "https://x.com/b")
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ov.operate.strategies.navigable_affordances(observation)

# _autosummary/ov.registry.html.md

# ov.registry

The plugin mechanism: decorated functions registered into a dict (§3.2).

Everything extensible in `ov` – probes (what we collect), analyzers (what we
conclude), and report sections (what we render) – is a callable registered with
declared `requires`/`produces` artifact dependencies. A run is then just:
*resolve registry -> topologically order by declared deps -> execute*. Adding a
new capability is registering a function; it never means editing a dispatcher
(open-closed).

This is the “functions as data” + dataflow-DAG shape the project favors. We keep
the `meshed` dependency optional by shipping a small, transparent topo-sort
here; a caller who wants `meshed` can build the same DAG from
[`Registry.items`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.Registry.items).

### Classes

| [`RegisteredFn`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.RegisteredFn)(name, fn[, requires, produces, ...])   | A registered callable plus its declared artifact-kind dependencies.                                                    |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Registry`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.Registry)(label)                                     | A named registry of [`RegisteredFn`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.RegisteredFn), with dependency-ordered resolution. |

### *class* ov.registry.RegisteredFn(name, fn, requires=(), produces=(), meta=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A registered callable plus its declared artifact-kind dependencies.

### *class* ov.registry.Registry(label)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A named registry of [`RegisteredFn`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.RegisteredFn), with dependency-ordered resolution.

```pycon
>>> reg = Registry("demo")
>>> @reg.register("a", produces=("x",))
... def a():
...     return "a"
>>> @reg.register("b", requires=("x",), produces=("y",))
... def b():
...     return "b"
>>> [r.name for r in reg.ordered()]   # b depends on a's output kind "x"
['a', 'b']
>>> reg["a"].fn()
'a'
```

#### *property* items *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [RegisteredFn](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.RegisteredFn)]*

The underlying `name -> RegisteredFn` mapping (read-only by convention).

#### names()

Registered names in insertion order.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### ordered(names=None)

Return the selected items topologically ordered by `requires`/`produces`.

An item depends on any *selected* item that `produces` a kind it
`requires`. Inputs produced by no selected item are treated as already
available (captured upstream). Falls back to selection order on a cycle.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`RegisteredFn`](_autosummary/ov.registry.html.md#ov.registry.RegisteredFn)]

#### register(name, , requires=(), produces=(), \*\*meta)

Decorator: register `fn` under `name` with its declared deps.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)], [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)]


# _autosummary/ov.reporting.html.md

# ov.reporting

Report layer: registered Markdown sections + the synopsis (Phase 2).

Each section is a registered function (`register_section()`) that takes the
analyses + run and returns a Markdown fragment; [`ov.reporting.render`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.render.html.md#module-ov.reporting.render)
concatenates the selected sections. [`ov.reporting.synopsis`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#module-ov.reporting.synopsis) performs the
structured map-reduce that compresses many findings into one agent-consumable
synopsis.

(The package is named `reporting` rather than `report` so it cannot shadow
the `ov.report` facade *function*; see `ov/__init__.py`.)

### Functions

| [`load_builtin_sections`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.html.md#ov.reporting.load_builtin_sections)()   | Import builtin report-section modules so their `@register_section` runs.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.reporting.load_builtin_sections()

Import builtin report-section modules so their `@register_section` runs.

Invoked once at the bottom of this module so the section registry is fully
populated on import (no order-dependent gaps). Safe to call repeatedly.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### Modules

| [`overview`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.overview.html.md#module-ov.reporting.overview)   | The `overview` one-liner: observe -> analyze -> report -> synopsis (§4).             |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`render`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.render.html.md#module-ov.reporting.render)       | Render Markdown report sections from an analyzed run (§8.3).                         |
| [`sections`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.sections.html.md#module-ov.reporting.sections)   | The default report sections (§8.3) -- each a registered Markdown fragment.           |
| [`synopsis`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#module-ov.reporting.synopsis)   | Synopsis: structured map-reduce over findings into one agent-consumable file (§8.4). |


# _autosummary/ov.reporting.overview.html.md

# ov.reporting.overview

The `overview` one-liner: observe -> analyze -> report -> synopsis (§4).

This is the pit-of-success entry point behind [`ov.overview()`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#ov.overview). It threads a
single store through capture, the deterministic analyzers, report rendering, and
the synopsis, returning the synopsis path/key. No model is involved.

### Functions

| [`run_overview`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.overview.html.md#ov.reporting.overview.run_overview)(url, \*[, headed, mode, probes, ...])   | Run the full deterministic pipeline and return the synopsis path/key.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.reporting.overview.run_overview(url, , headed=False, mode='reconstruct', probes='default', store=None, out_dir=None, authorized=None, lenses=('ux', 'arch'), baseline=None, \*\*observe_kw)

Run the full deterministic pipeline and return the synopsis path/key.

In `mode="review"` it inserts an own-target diff step between analysis and
reporting: the run is compared against a stored prior baseline (`baseline`,
or the latest prior run of the same target) so the review report and synopsis
carry regression/drift detail. A first review run (no baseline) is a no-op.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/ov.reporting.render.html.md

# ov.reporting.render

Render Markdown report sections from an analyzed run (§8.3).

Selects the registered sections that apply to the run’s mode, orders them by their
numeric `order`, renders each over the run + per-analyzer summaries, and writes
them to the store (and optionally an output directory). Returns the written keys
or paths.

### Functions

| [`render_reports`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.render.html.md#ov.reporting.render.render_reports)(run_or_analyses, \*[, ...])   | Render and persist the report sections; return their store keys/paths.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ov.reporting.render.render_reports(run_or_analyses, , sections='default', out_dir=None, store=None)

Render and persist the report sections; return their store keys/paths.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/ov.reporting.sections.html.md

# ov.reporting.sections

The default report sections (§8.3) – each a registered Markdown fragment.

A section is `fn(run, analyses) -> str`. Sections are registered with an
`order` (numeric prefix) and the `modes` they apply to (reconstruct/review),
so [`ov.reporting.render`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.render.html.md#module-ov.reporting.render) can select and concatenate them. They read the
already-analyzed [`CaptureRun`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.CaptureRun) (findings, fingerprint, api_surface,
rendering_model, …) plus the per-analyzer summaries – no model involved.

### Functions

| `api_section`(run, analyses)              |    |
|-------------------------------------------|----|
| `appendix_section`(run, analyses)         |    |
| `architecture_section`(run, analyses)     |    |
| `overview_section`(run, analyses)         |    |
| `reconstruction_section`(run, analyses)   |    |
| `recovered_source_section`(run, analyses) |    |
| `review_section`(run, analyses)           |    |
| `ux_section`(run, analyses)               |    |


# _autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md

# ov.reporting.synopsis

Synopsis: structured map-reduce over findings into one agent-consumable file (§8.4).

Maps each [`Finding`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.Finding) into a compact synopsis record, \*\*deduplicates
deterministically\*\* (cluster on type + evidence-ref overlap + normalized summary;
merge to the union of evidence refs and the max severity), and emits two
renderings from one source: `synopsis.json` (the SSOT a downstream agent
consumes) and `SYNOPSIS.md` derived from it (never hand-authored). Evidence-id
overlap is a model-free check, more reliable than LLM similarity-judging.

### Functions

| [`build_synopsis`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#ov.reporting.synopsis.build_synopsis)(run_or_id, \*[, out, store])   | Build + persist `synopsis.json` and the derived `SYNOPSIS.md`; return the md path/key.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`build_synopsis_doc`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#ov.reporting.synopsis.build_synopsis_doc)(run, \*[, diff])           | Build the `synopsis.json` SSOT document from a run's findings (pure).                    |
| [`dedupe_findings`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#ov.reporting.synopsis.dedupe_findings)(findings)                     | Cluster + merge findings deterministically; return synopsis records (pure).              |
| [`render_synopsis_md`](_autosummary/ov.reporting.synopsis.html.md#ov.reporting.synopsis.render_synopsis_md)(doc)                       | Derive SYNOPSIS.md from the synopsis JSON (never hand-authored).                         |

### ov.reporting.synopsis.build_synopsis(run_or_id, , out=None, store=None)

Build + persist `synopsis.json` and the derived `SYNOPSIS.md`; return the md path/key.

`run_or_id` may be a `CaptureRun` or a run id. The JSON is the SSOT;
the Markdown is derived. Both are written to the store (and `out` dir if given).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ov.reporting.synopsis.build_synopsis_doc(run, , diff=None)

Build the `synopsis.json` SSOT document from a run’s findings (pure).

When `diff` (a serialized [`RunDiff`](_autosummary/ov.base.html.md#ov.base.RunDiff)) is given – review mode
with a baseline – a `regression` block is appended so the synopsis tells a
downstream agent what changed since the prior run, not just the current state.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ov.reporting.synopsis.dedupe_findings(findings)

Cluster + merge findings deterministically; return synopsis records (pure).

Two findings cluster when they share `type` and either overlap on evidence
refs or share a normalized summary. Each cluster yields one record holding the
union of evidence refs, the max severity, and the highest-severity representative.

```pycon
>>> from ov.base import Finding, Severity
>>> a = Finding(type="ux_issue", signal="contrast.text", category="a11y",
...             title="low contrast", evidence_refs=["x"],
...             severity=Severity(impact_tier="serious", score=3.0))
>>> b = Finding(type="ux_issue", signal="contrast.text", category="a11y",
...             title="low contrast", evidence_refs=["y"],
...             severity=Severity(impact_tier="serious", score=5.0))
>>> recs = dedupe_findings([a, b])
>>> len(recs), sorted(recs[0]["evidence_refs"]), recs[0]["severity_score"]
(1, ['x', 'y'], 5.0)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### ov.reporting.synopsis.render_synopsis_md(doc)

Derive SYNOPSIS.md from the synopsis JSON (never hand-authored).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/ov.util.html.md

# ov.util

Internal helpers: content-addressing, hashing, redaction, and requirements.

Nothing here knows about Playwright or analysis specifics – these are the
small, reusable primitives the rest of the package leans on. The most
user-facing item is [`check_requirements()`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.check_requirements), which detects missing system
dependencies (Playwright browsers, Node, the sidecar, optional CLIs) and prints
the exact commands to install them, per the spec’s `check_requirements`
mandate (§9).

### Functions

| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.check_requirements)(\*[, components, verbose])   | Detect missing system dependencies and print exact install commands.           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`content_hash`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.content_hash)(data, \*[, length])                | Return a short, stable SHA-256 hex digest for content-addressing.              |
| [`redact_mapping`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.redact_mapping)(mapping, \*[, redact])           | Return a copy of `mapping` with values redacted when `redact` is true.         |
| [`redact_value`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.redact_value)(value)                             | Replace a value with a length-tagged placeholder (keeps shape, drops content). |
| [`sidecar_dir`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.sidecar_dir)()                                   | Return the path to the Node sidecar directory (`OV_SIDECAR_DIR` override).     |
| [`stable_hash`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.stable_hash)(obj, \*[, length])                  | Hash an arbitrary JSON-able object deterministically (sorted keys).            |

### Classes

| [`Requirement`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.Requirement)(name, present[, detail, ...])   | One checked system dependency.                                                                                        |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`RequirementReport`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.RequirementReport)([requirements])           | The result of [`check_requirements()`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.check_requirements) -- iterable, with a tidy summary. |

### *class* ov.util.Requirement(name, present, detail='', install_hint='', optional=True)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One checked system dependency.

### *class* ov.util.RequirementReport(requirements=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The result of [`check_requirements()`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.check_requirements) – iterable, with a tidy summary.

#### *property* missing *: [list](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[Requirement](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.Requirement)]*

Requirements that are absent (optional or not).

#### *property* ok *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True when every *non-optional* requirement is present.

#### render()

Human-readable multi-line summary with install hints for what’s missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ov.util.check_requirements(, components=None, verbose=True)

Detect missing system dependencies and print exact install commands.

`components` filters which groups to check (`"browser"`, `"node"`,
`"sidecar"`, `"clis"`); `None` checks all. The deterministic analysis
core needs none of these – they gate *capture* and the *arch sidecar*, so
every requirement here is reported as optional unless capture is requested.

```pycon
>>> rep = check_requirements(components=["clis"], verbose=False)
>>> isinstance(rep, RequirementReport)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`RequirementReport`](_autosummary/ov.util.html.md#ov.util.RequirementReport)

### ov.util.content_hash(data, , length=16)

Return a short, stable SHA-256 hex digest for content-addressing.

```pycon
>>> content_hash(b"hello")
'2cf24dba5fb0a30e'
>>> content_hash("hello") == content_hash(b"hello")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ov.util.redact_mapping(mapping, , redact=True)

Return a copy of `mapping` with values redacted when `redact` is true.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### ov.util.redact_value(value)

Replace a value with a length-tagged placeholder (keeps shape, drops content).

```pycon
>>> redact_value("super-secret-token")
'<redacted:18>'
>>> redact_value(None)
'<redacted>'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ov.util.sidecar_dir()

Return the path to the Node sidecar directory (`OV_SIDECAR_DIR` override).

Defaults to `<repo_root>/sidecar` (sibling of the `ov` package). Packaging
the sidecar for installed use is a later concern; for now it lives in the
source tree.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ov.util.stable_hash(obj, , length=16)

Hash an arbitrary JSON-able object deterministically (sorted keys).

Used for `obs_hash` and `args_hash` so progress detection is reproducible.

```pycon
>>> stable_hash({"b": 1, "a": 2}) == stable_hash({"a": 2, "b": 1})
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`ov` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ov-analyze-arch`

How to run ov’s deterministic architecture-reconstruction analyzers and turn the scored facts into a rebuild blueprint (reconstruct) or an architecture audit (review). Load this for the software-design lens: framework/rendering/state/routing detection, source-map recovery, API surface synthesis, dependency/CVE flags.

Source: [`.claude/skills/ov-analyze-arch`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/ov-analyze-arch).

### `ov-analyze-ux`

How to run ov’s deterministic UX + accessibility analyzers, assemble a grounded evidence bundle, and add narrative UX judgment as the host. Load this for the UX lens: accessibility audit, contrast, Core Web Vitals, form friction, Nielsen heuristics, and severity-ranked usability findings with fixes.

Source: [`.claude/skills/ov-analyze-ux`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/ov-analyze-ux).

### `ov-capture`

How to run an `ov` capture session against a web app — launch the browser, choose which probes to enable, and inspect the resulting artifact store. Load this when you are capturing a target with ov (step 1 of study-web-app), choosing probes, or looking at what was captured.

Source: [`.claude/skills/ov-capture`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/ov-capture).

### `ov-operate`

How to drive a web app with ov’s operate primitives — read affordances, choose and execute the next action, log per-step intent, and detect no-progress. Load this when you (the host) are driving a journey: crawling, pursuing a goal (signup/checkout), or replaying a script, and need the perceive→decide→act→record loop.

Source: [`.claude/skills/ov-operate`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/ov-operate).

### `ov-report`

How to render ov’s Markdown report sections and produce the single agent-consumable synopsis. Load this for the final step of study-web-app — turning analyzed findings into reports and a deduplicated synopsis.json + SYNOPSIS.md.

Source: [`.claude/skills/ov-report`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/ov-report).

### `study-web-app`

Study, audit, reverse-engineer, or review a web app or website end-to-end with the `ov` tool. Use whenever the user says things like “go study this app”, “audit this site’s UX”, “reconstruct this frontend”, “what’s this site built with”, “review our web app”, “analyze the accessibility of this page”, or hands you a URL to investigate. You (the host agent) are the manager: you plan the journey, call ov’s deterministic tools, reason over the grounded evidence, and assemble the report. ov supplies the hands (drive) and eyes (observe + analyze); you supply the control loop.

Source: [`.claude/skills/study-web-app`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/.claude/skills/study-web-app).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ov/tree/HEAD/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ov/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`ov.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ov/ov.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/ov/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)

# API reference

| [`ov`](_autosummary/ov.html.md#module-ov)   | `ov` -- OverView: agent-driven web reconnaissance & analysis.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
